description: Three fail-open advisory hooks: (1) UserPromptSubmit nudge deterministically steers Claude toward the nexus.memory_create / nexus.context_retrieve MCP tools on cross-session memory write/read intent (lifetime-axis rules shared with skills/nexus-memory/SKILL.md via hooks/rules.json); (2) SessionStart injection warm-starts a fresh session with the project's recent settled summaries (cross-container, provenance-annotated) via context/retrieve; (3) SessionEnd capture distills the session transcript into bounded activities and POSTs them to /activities/stream (P1 write side; backend worker extracts episodic memory keyed user_id=project). All are advisory only — never block the prompt, session startup, or teardown; fail-open exit 0. TWO FIELDS BELOW ARE LOAD-BEARING, do not tidy them away: SessionEnd `timeout: 60` — Claude Code gives all SessionEnd hooks a SHARED 1.5 s budget unless one declares a longer timeout (then the budget is raised to match, capped at 60), and the capture hook's own HTTP timeout is 8 s; SessionStart `matcher: startup|resume` — compact and clear also fire SessionStart, and re-injecting there spends a retrieval on a session that already has the brief. SessionStart `timeout: 30` is a backstop, not the mechanism; the default would be 600. Both session hooks keep a deadline of their own (25 s and 20 s) and cap the ledger write at 2 s, so that they record `timeout` and exit 0 by themselves: a hook the host has to kill leaves no ledger record, and for SessionStart its stdout is discarded. A test keeps each `timeout` above deadline + ledger cap, read from the code. (urllib timeouts are per socket operation, not per request, which is why the hooks cannot rely on them.)
